QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_4

question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund's manager is breaking down the Investor Due Diligence scope for a planned anchor position. Which of the following correctly maps the three standard IDD components?

answer.text: (i) Treasury DD, (ii) HR DD, (iii) Marketing DD
(i) Tax DDR, (ii) ESG DDR, (iii) Cyber DDR
(i) Business/Commercial/Technical DDR, (ii) Financial DDR, (iii) Legal DDR
(i) Sponsor DDR, (ii) Trustee DDR, (iii) Distributor DDR

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter defines IDD as having three standard components: (a) Business, Commercial and Technical DDR; (b) Financial DDR (covering books, financial statements, direct and indirect tax); (c) Legal DDR (legal aspects, IPR, contracts, litigation, statutory compliance). The Trap: The wrong options mix unrelated verticals or swap names of governance participants for DDR buckets. Tax is a SUB-COMPONENT of Financial DDR, not a standalone stream in this framework. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D cover identical IDD taxonomy since chapter text is shared. Distinguish from 'Investor-side DD' that XXI-A/B candidates perform on the manager. Manager's Pro-Tip: On Cat III desks running merger-arb, assign Business DDR (deal rationale) to the internal team, Financial DDR to Big-4 (covenant testing, net debt) and Legal DDR to a transaction-law firm (SPA reps & warranties) — parallel-track them to hit the deal close window.
